title: Bonjour tout le monde
oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic greetings in French
decisionPoints: How comfortable do students seem with hearing French?
Do they need more gesture and visual support?
Should we repeat greetings more times?
progression: First exposure to French sounds and basic social interaction

title: Comment tu t'appelles?
oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What's your name?' and hear name responses
decisionPoints: Are students ready to attempt saying their names in French?
Do they understand the question through context?
How much wait time do they need?
progression: Builds on greetings by adding personal identification

title: Les couleurs magiques
oneGoal: Students will recognize and point to basic colors when named in French
decisionPoints: Which colors are students most confident with?
Do they need more hands-on color activities?
Are visual supports sufficient?
progression: Introduces concrete vocabulary that connects to their world

title: Compter ensemble
oneGoal: Students will recognize numbers 1-5 in French through songs and games
decisionPoints: Are students following the counting pattern?
Do they need more kinesthetic number activities?
Should we focus on fewer numbers today?
progression: Adds mathematical concepts while reinforcing listening skills

title: Ma famille
oneGoal: Students will identify family members when shown pictures and hear French names
decisionPoints: How are students connecting to family vocabulary?
Do they need more time to process these words?
Are they ready to share about their families?
progression: Connects to personal experiences while reviewing previous vocabulary

title: J'aime les animaux
oneGoal: Students will recognize common animal names and show preference with 'j'aime'
decisionPoints: Can students differentiate between the animal sounds?
Are they ready to express preferences?
Do they understand 'j'aime' through modeling?
progression: Introduces expressing preferences while spiraling colors and numbers

title: Dans ma classe
oneGoal: Students will identify and point to classroom objects when named
decisionPoints: Can students locate objects around the room?
Do they need more physical movement with vocabulary?
Are they connecting French words to familiar objects?
progression: Builds practical vocabulary for daily classroom interactions

title: Les parties du corps
oneGoal: Students will touch body parts when named and follow simple 'Touchez...' commands
decisionPoints: Are students following the action commands?
Do they need slower pacing for body movements?
Should we add more body parts or consolidate these?
progression: Introduces action words while building body awareness vocabulary

title: Qu'est-ce que c'est?
oneGoal: Students will understand the question 'What is it?' and hear simple responses
decisionPoints: Do students recognize the questioning pattern?
Are they ready to attempt responses?
How much scaffolding do they need for 'c'est'?
progression: Introduces question-answer patterns using known vocabulary

title: Où est...?
oneGoal: Students will understand location questions and respond through pointing/gestures
decisionPoints: Can students follow the location game?
Do they understand spatial concepts in French?
Are they ready for more complex hide-and-seek activities?
progression: Builds on question patterns while adding spatial awareness

title: Les émotions
oneGoal: Students will recognize emotion words and connect them to facial expressions
decisionPoints: Can students match emotions to expressions?
Are they comfortable expressing how they feel?
Do they need more emotion vocabulary or focus on these three?
progression: Introduces emotional vocabulary while practicing 'je suis' structure

title: À l'école
oneGoal: Students will understand school-related vocabulary and simple school rules
decisionPoints: Do students connect these words to their school experience?
Are they ready to hear simple classroom expectations in French?
How well are they following along with longer phrases?
progression: Connects learning to their school environment using familiar concepts

title: Mes vêtements
oneGoal: Students will identify clothing items and understand 'Je porte...' statements
decisionPoints: Can students identify clothing on themselves/others?
Are they understanding the 'je porte' structure?
Do they need more time with clothing vocabulary?
progression: Builds personal description skills while practicing 'je' statements

title: La nourriture
oneGoal: Students will recognize food vocabulary and express simple preferences
decisionPoints: Are students connecting food words to real experiences?
Can they express food preferences using 'j'aime'?
Do they need more concrete food examples?
progression: Spirals 'j'aime' with new vocabulary category relevant to daily life

title: Les saisons
oneGoal: Students will identify seasons and connect them to weather and activities
decisionPoints: Do students understand season concepts in French?
Can they connect weather words to their experiences?
Are they ready to discuss seasonal activities?
progression: Introduces environmental vocabulary while reviewing descriptive words

title: Je peux...
oneGoal: Students will use 'je peux' to express what they can do with learned vocabulary
decisionPoints: Are students ready to create their own sentences?
How much support do they need with 'je peux' structure?
Can they combine actions with previously learned vocabulary?
progression: Consolidates learning by having students express abilities using known words

title: Mon histoire
oneGoal: Students will share simple personal information using learned vocabulary and structures
decisionPoints: Are students confident enough to attempt sharing?
How much scaffolding do they need for personal expression?
Should we focus on specific vocabulary categories?
progression: Encourages creative use of all learned vocabulary in personal context

title: Nos amis
oneGoal: Students will describe classmates using learned vocabulary and practice social language
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable describing others positively?
Can they use descriptive words appropriately?
Do they understand the social nature of this vocabulary?
progression: Applies learned vocabulary to peer relationships and social interactions

title: Notre classe française
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their French learning through a simple class presentation or show
decisionPoints: How can each student contribute to the class celebration?
What vocabulary are they most confident with?
How can we celebrate individual growth within the group?
progression: Celebrates collective learning and builds confidence for continued French study

title: Au revoir septembre
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their French learning journey and set intentions for continued learning
decisionPoints: What French words/phrases are students most proud of learning?
How can we bridge to future French learning?
What connections have students made with French culture/language?
progression: Consolidates the unit while preparing students for ongoing French immersion journey
